Article Title: Elon Musk has a six-word reply for CEO of America's largest mobile network company who said SpaceX needs eight years to build a rival network
Article Text:
Verizon CEO gave SpaceX 8 years. Musk says 3

Verizon CEO says Starlink satellites can't compete in cities

Starlink Mobile would be the sixth player in US wireless, not the fourth

Verizon CEO Dan Schulman thinks SpaceX has a long way to go if it wants to compete with America's big mobile carriers. On Verizon's third-quarter earnings call on Monday, he said SpaceX would need $300 billion to $500 billion, up to 80,000 cell towers and as long as eight years to build a network that could match Verizon's. Elon Musk replied quickly. "Will take 2 or 3 years," the SpaceX CEO posted on X after the call.The exchange comes at a tense time for US telecom companies. Earlier this month, SpaceX bought low-band spectrum in a deal worth about $8 billion. These airwaves work well for phones, and the news sent Verizon's shares down nearly 9% in one day, the stock's worst day since 2002. SpaceX is also reportedly working to secure at least 80,000 cell sites across the US, and it has approached tower owners including Crown Castle.Schulman did not dismiss Musk. He said he works on the assumption that SpaceX will do everything it says it will do, and "execute flawlessly". His argument was that satellites alone cannot match a ground network in cities and suburbs, which account for about 98% of Verizon's revenue. "We're somewhere between 100 to 1000 times more efficient than they are," he said.To close that gap, Schulman said, SpaceX would need 65,000 to 80,000 large tower sites, along with backhaul, radio equipment and more spectrum.He estimated the build would take at least four to six years, with spending spread over seven or eight. Retail stores, customer service and back-office systems would come after that."There is no magic wand. There is no shortcut," he said.Schulman added that even a finished network would make SpaceX the sixth competitor in the US market, not the fourth. Verizon's network already carries Spectrum Mobile and Xfinity Mobile, two large cable-backed operators. He also ruled out renting Verizon's network to SpaceX through a wholesale deal, saying he sees no benefit in offering one to a satellite provider."It's very hard to throw a punch against something that doesn't exist. But once they come into the market, we will be ferociously competitive," he said.SpaceX plans to switch on Starlink Mobile in early 2028, using next-generation satellites, ground towers and small home cells. Last week, Musk told investors that Starlink connectivity could eventually bring in several hundred billion dollars a year.Verizon is not the only carrier playing down the threat. Last week, AT&T CEO John Stankey said he "wouldn't over-rotate" on one carrier's low-band spectrum.Verizon's own quarter was strong. The company added 406,000 postpaid phone customers and raised its full-year earnings forecast.
Article Summary: Verizon CEO says SpaceX would need $300 billion to $500 billion to build a network. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk replied: "Will take 2 or 3 years" The exchange comes at a tense time for US telecom companies. Earlier this month, SpaceX bought low-band spectrum in a deal worth about $8 billion.

Article Title: China's Alibaba wins court ruling over Pentagon ban that made the company fire dozens of American lobby firms
Article Text:
China's Alibaba wins court ruling over Pentagon ban that made the company fire dozens of American lobby firms

What the ruling means for Alibaba

BYD, DJI and other Chinese companies on Pentagon’s blacklist

A US federal judge has ruled that the government cannot block companies from getting Pentagon contracts simply because they work with firms that lobby for Alibaba, reports Reuters. The Chinese company sued the US government in June this year after the Pentagon added the Chinese company to a list of firms accused of helping China’s military. The list also included search engine company Baidu, electric vehicle maker BYD and other Chinese technology and manufacturing firms.The court’s decision allows Alibaba to continue working with Washington lobbyists who also represent companies that do business with the Pentagon. As per the report, this could help the Chinese company fight its inclusion on the US military-related list.Alibaba reportedly dropped dozens of lobbyists after the Pentagon named it in June. The company has challenged the decision, arguing that there is no evidence to support the claim that it has links to China’s military.Being on the list does not bring direct sanctions, but it can affect a company’s ability to secure Pentagon contracts.From 2027, restrictions are also expected to cover purchases of listed companies’ products and services through other suppliers, potentially affecting their place in US defence supply chains.Alibaba says its technology is built for businesses, retail and logistics, not military or intelligence work. The latest court order, however, does not remove the company from the Pentagon’s list. Its legal challenge is still ongoing.Notably, Alibaba is not the only Chinese firm on the Pentagon’s blacklist. Last month, two subsidiaries ​of the world's largest electric ​vehicle maker BYD also sued ⁠the US Department of Defence over a federal law banning any Pentagon contractors from hiring lobbyists that also work with blacklisted firms.Earlier in August, DJI appealed its inclusion on the blacklist. The same month, biotech firm WuXi ​AppTec Co also won a preliminary injunction from a US federal court, that blocked its inclusion on the list.
Article Summary: Alibaba sued the US government in June after the Pentagon added the Chinese company to a list of firms accused of helping China’s military. The list also included search engine company Baidu, electric vehicle maker BYD and other Chinese technology and manufacturing firms. A US federal judge has ruled that the government cannot block companies from getting Pentagon contracts simply because they work with firms that lobby for Alibaba.

Article Title: Republicans and Democrats may reportedly agree on message for AI company CEOs: They need to shut up
Article Text:
Republicans and Democrats may reportedly agree on message for AI company CEOs: They need to shut up

AI CEOs warn of existential risks

Lawmakers, hill staffers and Washington insiders in both Republicans and Democrats are reportedly seeing AI as a ‘political liability’, sources told Axios. The parties, as per the report, has a uniform message for AI CEOs: “put a sock in it and just build their products — safely”. “CEOs like Sam Altman are saying the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology,” Republican Ro Khanna told the publication. “You cannot trust billionaires to make decisions to keep us safe.”The report cited Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) who said: “The American people hate that Donald Trump is cozying up to tech billionaires, while AI threatens our jobs and livelihoods. Democrats need to make the AI industry's political money an issue, data centers an issue, and go on offense to protect workers and kids.”As stated in the Axios report, lawmakers and regulators believe that AI industry leaders are complicating the debate over regulation by shifting public attention between the technology’s promise of economic prosperity and warnings about existential risks. “Rather than leading the charge to persuade Americans about the benefits of AI, and the potential for shared prosperity — the core elements of any winning political campaign — industry leaders are constantly warning of its existential dangers,” it says.Lawmakers, as per the report, say AI executives often alternate between messages of economic opportunity and warnings of potential doom, sometimes during the same public appearances. They argue that these conflicting messages add to political uncertainty at a time when public backlash against AI is already growing. This in turn has left regulators wondering whether “that's a feature or a bug”.“We can all speculate on what's going on, but all it does is have everybody wake up Monday morning and say 'these guys are awful, we've had enough,'” one source citing conversations with Hill offices told Axios.The report quoted Senator John Curtis (R-Utah) who said “It's obvious that they're tripping over their own shoelaces in trying to sell the value of this to the public. t's very hard to imagine a group right now that operates more in a vacuum, more out of touch with everyday Americans, than the AI industry.”"Your instinct is to wreak havoc on the public SI discourse," Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) said in a letter to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei earlier this month, complaining about Amodei's "panic-inducing commentary."
Article Summary: Lawmakers, hill staffers and Washington insiders in both Republicans and Democrats are reportedly seeing AI as a ‘political liability’ The parties, as per the report, has a uniform message for AI CEOs: “put a sock in it and just build their products — safely”

Article Title: Claude AI now writes over 90% of the code at Anthropic; company in its IPO filing says: The job of an engineer at Anthropic is now to
Article Text:
Pages from the Anthropic website and the company's logo are displayed on a computer screen in New York on Thursday, Feb. 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Patrick Sison)

Anthropic is using Claude to build the next version of Claude

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei predicted the 90% mark more than a year and a half ago

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe AI should take on more coding tasks in the future? Yes, definitely Maybe No, it shouldn't 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Anthropic's own AI now writes most of the software inside the company. Claude produced more than 90% of the contributions to Anthropic's codebase in September, according to the company's S-1 filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The 335-page document, filed on October 26, sets Anthropic up for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker "ANT", possibly as early as next month.The filing also shows how the job of an Anthropic engineer has changed. Its software engineers now mostly direct and review Claude's output instead of writing code line by line. The numbers back it up: average daily code contributions per engineer in the July to September quarter were more than 45 times their average daily level in 2024.Coding is only one part of a wider shift. Anthropic says it now relies on its models to research, design and develop the models that come after them, a process the company calls closing the loop. Claude runs experiments, generates training data, and automates evaluations and safety audits. It has also helped with algorithmic improvements that let Anthropic get more out of its computing resources."Claude itself has become one of the most powerful drivers of our progress," the company wrote in the filing.That reliance shapes hiring too. Anthropic's workforce grew from about 940 employees at the end of 2024 to roughly 5,300 by late September, and the company says its strategy is to keep growing the business without adding staff at the same pace. A recent internal report noted that it has been filling a smaller share of junior technical positions as AI agents take on coding, bug fixes and similar tasks. Regrettable attrition, meanwhile, stood at about 1% for the 12 months ending September 30.The figure will not surprise anyone who has followed CEO Dario Amodei. In March 2025, he said AI would be writing 90% of code within three to six months, and could be writing essentially all of it within a year. By October that year, he told an audience at Salesforce's Dreamforce conference that the number already held true within Anthropic. He also argued that companies might end up needing more engineers, since each one becomes far more productive with AI doing the bulk of the typing.Some teams inside the company have gone even further. Boris Cherny, who heads Claude Code, said in June that he had not written a line of code by hand in about eight months.The filing pairs all this with a note of caution. Among its long list of risk factors, Anthropic warns that its AI systems may behave in unintended, misaligned or autonomous ways that could damage the business. That is the same system now responsible for nine in every ten contributions to the company's codebase, and increasingly, for helping build the next Claude.
Article Summary: Anthropic's own AI now writes most of the software inside the company. CEO Dario Amodei predicted the 90% mark more than a year and a half ago. Anthropic says it now relies on its models to research, design and develop the models that come after them.

Article Title: Our priority is to build FFI into a lasting part of the country’s gaming community: Vaibhav Das Mundhra, head of operations, India, Garena
Article Text:
Vaibhav Das Mundhra, head of operations, India, Garena

Garena already has Free Fire Max as one of the most popular mobile action games in India. How does Free Fire India make a difference to users in India?

How is Garena balancing an engaging player experience with measures that encourage healthy gaming habits, particularly among younger audiences?

Data security and regulatory compliance have become important considerations for digital platforms in India. How have these considerations shaped Garena's approach to developing and operating Free Fire India?

As competitive gaming continues to grow in India, how does Garena see the role of grassroots and collegiate competitions in developing Indian esports talent and creating opportunities to compete internationally?

Looking ahead, what are Garena's priorities for Free Fire India, and how does the company envision strengthening its engagement with India's gaming community, including players, creators and esports talent?

Garena has announced the availability of Free Fire India (FFI) starting October 28. Available as a standalone app on the App Store and Google Play, FFI, according to the company, will offer exciting gameplay, opportunities to connect with friends and locally relevant content. On Free Fire India's launch, Times of India spoke to Vaibhav Das Mundhra, head of operations, India, Garena on the game and the company's India plans.Free Fire India (FFI) is a new standalone app developed specifically for mobile gamers in India, offering fast-paced gameplay, an engaging social experience and broad device accessibility. We have optimised FFI to run smoothly on a wide range of smartphones, including lower-specification devices, making the game accessible to more players across India. Free Fire MAX will remain as a separate app for players using higher-specification devices. For us, bringing FFI to players is also a way to build on our relationship with India’s gaming community over the years. As part of this, we will be introducing an in-game Diwali campaign, featuring localised bundles.We have built several safeguards into FFI to support responsible gameplay and help players maintain a healthy balance. These include age-verification features, with users under 18 needing consent from a parent or guardian before creating an account, regular break reminders, and defined playtime limits, which is up to 6 hours per day for users above 18 and up to 3 hours for users under 18. Spending caps will apply to users under 18, while in-game purchases remain optional. Some visual effects have also been modified, with red blood and certain other effects removed or replaced.We are committed to promoting responsible gameplay and fostering positive community engagement. Through “Play It Right”, we devote significant resources to helping FFI players develop healthy gaming habits and contribute to a supportive gaming community. The initiative focuses on developing educational and short-video content, relatable comics, break reminder notifications breaks, limiting playtime, and focusing on their overall well-being. These safeguards are part of how we are building a more responsible environment for players and families, while allowing the community to enjoy the game in a healthy and balanced way.When we prepared FFI for availability in India, data protection and local requirements were important considerations for us. The game will be hosted on servers in India, and sensitive personal data of Indian users related to FFI will be stored locally in India. We have also taken feedback from relevant government authorities into account as we prepared the game for players here. Our focus is on protecting player data and operating in line with applicable Indian laws and regulations.In developing and operating FFI, we also draw on Garena’s development expertise across markets, with a local team in India supporting the game’s marketing and operations.We believe grassroots and collegiate competitions play an important role in nurturing Indian esports talent. These tournaments provide aspiring players and teams with opportunities to hone their skills, gain competitive experience, and progress through different levels of competition.Our priority is to build FFI into a lasting part of the country’s gaming community. This starts with delivering a familiar, engaging experience tailored to players in India, while encouraging safe and responsible play. We will continue developing the game in ways that give players more opportunities to enjoy themselves and connect with one another.We are grateful for the support players, creators, and competitive gaming communities have shown us over the years, and hope to continue building on these relationships. Our local team will support marketing and operations, helping us stay attuned to the needs and interests of the community. We will also continue to explore in-game campaigns that celebrate India's diverse cultures and communities.We see this as a long-term effort, and look forward to sharing more about future initiatives as they take shape.
Article Summary: Free Fire India (FFI) is a new standalone app developed specifically for mobile gamers in India. Available as a standalone app on the App Store and Google Play, FFI, according to the company, will offer exciting gameplay, opportunities to connect with friends and locally relevant content.

Article Title: Dyson study finds 1 in 2 Indians frequently miss cleaning under beds and furniture
Article Text: More than half of Indian households are missing hard-to-reach areas such as spaces under beds and furniture during routine cleaning, according to Dyson's first 'How India Cleans' study. The survey also found that hair left behind on floors and dust quickly resettling after cleaning remain among the biggest frustrations for consumers. The study, conducted among over 650 respondents across seven Indian cities, examines how Indians clean their homes, the challenges they face and what they expect from modern floorcare technology. According to the findings, 52% of respondents said spaces beneath beds and furniture are frequently missed during cleaning, while 48% reported difficulties cleaning corners, edges and skirting areas.Despite significant time spent on household cleaning, many consumers continue to struggle with achieving a thorough clean. Dyson said more than half of respondents spend between 30 minutes and an hour cleaning floors, while another 11% spend up to two hours.The study highlights that the issue is not just how often people clean, but whether existing cleaning tools can effectively tackle different surfaces and hard-to-reach spaces throughout the home.According to the survey, 36% of respondents identified human or pet hair left behind on floors as one of their biggest cleaning pain points. Meanwhile, 38% said dust settles again quickly after cleaning, creating the impression that surfaces become dirty soon after they have been cleaned. Dyson noted that household dust can easily become airborne due to everyday activity before resettling on surfaces, making effective dust removal a continuing challenge.The study found that Indian households often feature a mix of flooring types that require different cleaning approaches. While hard flooring remains common, 72% of respondents said they also have carpets and rugs at home. Other common surfaces include marble (51%), vitrified or ceramic tiles (49%), and granite (43%). This diversity means consumers increasingly seek cleaning solutions that can move seamlessly across different floor types without compromising performance.When selecting floorcare products, respondents indicated a strong preference for advanced technology. Around 61% said better technology influenced their purchase decisions, ahead of cleaning performance (54%) and brand trust (49%). In comparison, only 21% cited pricing and promotional offers as a key factor. The survey also found that vacuum cleaners are increasingly being used for whole-home cleaning rather than just floor maintenance. Respondents reported using them under furniture (71%), on hard floors (70%), carpets and rugs (69%), upholstery (69%), and beds and mattresses (63%).Commenting on the findings, Tim Hare, Design and Development Engineer, Floor Care at Dyson, said consumers increasingly expect vacuum cleaners to tackle multiple cleaning challenges in a single session, ranging from fine dust and long hair to different floor surfaces and hard-to-reach areas. The company said insights from the study help shape the development of future floorcare products by identifying real-world cleaning problems and unmet consumer needs.Alongside the study, Dyson highlighted its recently launched Dyson V16 Piston Animal cordless vacuum cleaner, priced at ₹79,900. The company said the device is designed to address common household cleaning challenges through features such as automatic floor-type sensing, anti-tangle technology for long hair, LED illumination for spotting hidden dust, and up to 70 minutes of fade-free suction.The appliance also includes Dyson's CleanCompaktor bin technology, which the company claims can compress dust and debris to increase storage capacity and reduce the frequency of emptying. The findings underscore a growing consumer focus on cleaning effectiveness rather than just effort, with many households seeking technology-driven solutions that can deliver a more complete clean across modern homes.
Article Summary: More than half of Indian households are missing hard-to-reach areas such as spaces under beds and furniture during routine cleaning. The survey also found that hair left behind on floors and dust quickly resettling after cleaning remain among the biggest frustrations for consumers. The study was conducted among over 650 respondents across seven Indian cities.

Article Title: Elon Musk has a 'failure warning' for these technology companies; says: Investors have already started betting against them
Article Text:
Elon Musk has a 'failure warning' for these technology companies; says: Investors have already started betting against them

What are neoclouds

“As someone with a portfolio of energized land assets here is what I am seeing:

1. Neoclouds are disorganized and poorly capitalized. Some are definitely better than others however.

2. Hyperscalers are intractable, bureaucratic organizations that take 3 months to do an NDA and want 18mo escrow periods. We built our portfolio by competing against these terms because of our speed and simplicity.

The more future assets orgs like ours win, the bigger the problem for the hyperscalers downstream (see 3).

3. There are delays in the existing pipeline that will catch people off guard in 2027. Hyperacalers will (obviously) react by focusing on their own internal compute needs over any third party. If the third party is a model company, they will tell them to go through their model router where they will also take a non-trivial vig.

Them telling Ant they have no compute for them (rumored in Ant’s S-1) if true is a huge tell that this is already happening.

All of this is to say that it does look like there will be a lot of partially stranded compute and compute sitting in inventory in 2027 than is currently forecasted. This is bought and paid for but effectively underearning (below total cost of capital) or collecting dust. We see this as true for everyone - model companies, hyperscalers, neoclouds except ONE (you can guess which one).

This dislocation will benefit two kinds of orgs: the non-bureaucratic big scalers who can build industrial scale quickly and the nimble, well capitalized players feeding them.

2027 will be a turbulent year because it will clear out a bunch of wrong/bad bets. It will also be a consolidation year for a few.”
Article Summary: 2027 will be a turbulent year because it will clear out a bunch of wrong/bad bets. The more future assets orgs like ours win, the bigger the problem for the hyperscalers downstream. There are delays in the existing pipeline that will catch people off guard in 2027.

Article Title: PhonePe launches Tatkal NPS, enables instant pension account opening with Rs 250 investment
Article Text:
How users can open a Tatkal NPS account on PhonePe

PhonePe has launched ‘Tatkal NPS’ on its platform in partnership with leading banking institutions, allowing users to open a National Pension System (NPS) account digitally and begin retirement planning with contributions starting at Rs 250. The digital payments and financial services company said the new offering is aimed at making long-term retirement planning more accessible to millions of Indians through a fully digital and paperless onboarding process. The service enables users to create a government-backed pension account and obtain a Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) within minutes without the need for fresh document uploads or additional KYC procedures.According to PhonePe, the Tatkal NPS service allows customers to complete account opening in three simple steps by leveraging existing bank KYC records. The platform has integrated with leading banks to facilitate seamless onboarding, with plans to broaden coverage across the banking sector in the future. The initiative is powered by the Tatkal NPS framework developed by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).Under this mechanism, users can authenticate themselves through a one-time password (OTP) linked to their bank account, enabling secure reuse of existing KYC details. This eliminates paperwork and significantly reduces the time required to open an NPS account.PhonePe said the offering is designed to appeal to a wide spectrum of users, including first-time financial planners, millennials and Gen-Z consumers. By lowering the minimum contribution amount to Rs 250, the company aims to encourage early retirement planning among younger Indians.The company also highlighted that the service could be particularly useful for gig workers, freelancers and small business owners who may not have access to employer-sponsored retirement benefits. The micro-investment approach is intended to make disciplined retirement savings more accessible to individuals across income segments.Users can access the service by searching for “NPS” within the PhonePe app and selecting the National Pension Scheme option. They can then start the pension account journey, choose their linked bank account, authenticate it using a bank OTP, and make an initial contribution starting from Rs 250 through PhonePe UPI. Once the process is completed, a PRAN is generated instantly.With the launch of Tatkal NPS, PhonePe is expanding its financial services portfolio while seeking to drive greater participation in formal retirement savings among India's growing digital user base.
Article Summary: PhonePe has launched ‘Tatkal NPS’ on its platform in partnership with leading banking institutions. Users can open a National Pension System (NPS) account digitally and begin retirement planning with contributions starting at Rs 250. The service enables users to create a government-backed pension account.

Article Title: Meta plans to raise up to $95 billion for its AI expansion through two stock offerings, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom interested in buying shares as Mark Zuckerberg seeks new funding without surrender
Article Text:
Silicon suppliers eye $5 billion stake amid ‘Circular Capital’ concerns

Big Tech pivots to equity and debt to fund compute

Facebook-parent company Meta announced on Monday (October 26) that it plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising effort, seeking fresh capital to fuel its massive artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure expansion without diluting CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s voting control. The capital plan consists of two separate equity moves. The first is that the company has rolled out public offerings valued at roughly $35 billion in common and preferred stock, and second, it intends to establish a separate at-the-market share sale program worth up to $60 billion.Meta said the larger, $60 billion program will be deployed after its newly created non-voting Class C shares commence public trading—expected in the first quarter of 2027. Specific timelines and transaction terms for that phase have not yet been finalized.The fundraising plan, which is marking one of the largest financial hauls ever attempted by an AI company, has already attracted serious interest from its primary semiconductor hardware partners. Top chipmakers Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and Broadcom are collectively looking to acquire up to $5 billion in Meta's voting Class A shares.While the move guarantees immediate institutional backing, it has renewed scrutiny over a circular flow of capital within the AI sector, where primary hardware vendors help bankroll the rapid infrastructure build-out of one of their largest enterprise customers. Meta has been pouring billions into advanced accelerators and specialized server campuses to keep pace with rival AI developers OpenAI and Anthropic.Meta’s massive share offering reflects a broader industry-wide shift among technology heavyweights, which are turning to public debt markets and share sales to sustain their computing appetite rather than relying solely on balance-sheet cash reserves.Earlier this year, Google parent Alphabet expanded the scope of its own equity offerings to $84.75 billion.On the same day as Meta's disclosure, Elon Musk's SpaceX revealed that an affiliate of private equity giant Apollo Global Management will purchase AI processors and data center hardware before leasing the equipment back to the firm, in a transaction totaling approximately $40 billion in principal payments.Notably, Meta has committed to roughly $825 billion in future expenditures, an enormous capital pipeline driven by new data center builds, cloud computing access, and next-generation server clusters. But clearly, that aggressive operational tempo has taken a toll on the company's financial profile.
Article Summary: Big Tech pivots to equity and debt to fund compute infrastructure expansion. Top chipmakers Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and Broadcom are collectively looking to acquire up to $5 billion in Meta's voting Class A shares. Meta has committed to roughly $825 billion in future expenditures.

Article Title: Apple releases macOS 27.2 Golden Gate: Features, how to download and more
Article Text:
Apple releases macOS 27.2 Golden Gate

How to download macOS 27.2 Golden Gate

Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner of your screen.

Open System Settings.

Click General and select Software Update.

Wait for your MacBook to check for available updates.

If macOS 27.2 Golden Gate is available for your device, click Upgrade Now or Update Now.

Enter your administrator password if prompted and follow the on-screen instructions to complete the installation.

macOS 27 Golden Gate features

A rebuilt search index for Spotlight, Photos and Mail

Apple has released latest macOS 27.2 Golden Gate software, marking the first major update to macOS 27 since its launch in September this year. Among other changes, the update brings changes to brightness and volume sliders. It also expands Siri AI to new languages including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. In its release notes, Apple said: “This update provides enhancements to Siri AI with the ability to retain useful context from previous Siri interactions as well as draw from a wider range of personal context. It also introduces Suggestions in Messages that help you take quick actions in apps like Calendar and Reminders based on context from your conversation. This release includes additional features, bug fixes, and security updates for your Mac”.To download the macOS 27.2 Golden Gate on your MacBook, follow the steps below:First announced at WWDC in June this year, the macOS 27 Golden Gate software update features a transparency slider that runs from completely clear to fully tinted, so you pick your poison. Sidebars stretch to the edge of the window with refraction continuing underneath them, sidebar icons keep their colour, and every window shares the same corner radius—even apps that haven't been updated.App icons pick up extra Liquid Glass layers built directly into the artwork.The plumbing behind Spotlight, Photos and Mail has been rearchitected. New stuff gets indexed almost immediately rather than disappearing into the void for hours, and a full reindex runs once after you update. Should fix the "why can't Finder find this file I made twenty minutes ago" problem that's dogged Tahoe.Siri AI lands on the Mac too—the Gemini-collaborated version, with onscreen awareness, personal context, and its own app. It's wired into Spotlight, so you can summon it from the same place you'd hunt for a file. Right-click on any window or item to ask Siri about it directly, or select multiple files in Finder and have it compare them for you. Conversation history syncs across devices via iCloud, so a thread you start on the Mac picks up on the iPhone or Watch.
Article Summary: macOS 27.2 Golden Gate features a rebuilt search index for Spotlight, Photos and Mail. Gemini-collaborated version of Siri adds onscreen awareness, personal context, and its own app. Sidebars stretch to the edge of the window with refraction continuing underneath them.

Article Title: Stanford economists have a warning for California on its proposed Billionaires' Tax; says it may leave the State poorer by ...
Article Text:
What Proposition 40 would do

Revenue estimate far below supporters' projections

Why researchers forecast a $39 billion loss

‘Billionaires can move’

Other economists disagree

Fierce political battle underway

California's proposed billionaire tax could generate far less revenue than supporters project and may ultimately leave the state nearly $39 billion worse off, according to a new analysis by two economists affiliated with Stanford University's Hoover Institution. According to a report by Fortune, the warning comes as voters prepare to decide on Proposition 40 in the 3 November election. The ballot measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of California residents who were billionaires as of 1 January 2026, with supporters claiming it could raise about $100 billion for the state, around 90% of which would be directed toward healthcare spending.The measure is on California’s November 3 ballot. It would impose a one-time 5 percent tax on the net worth of the state’s few hundred billionaires who were residents on January 1, 2026, with payment due in 2027. Those who choose to spread payments over five years would pay more. Real estate, pensions and most retirement accounts would generally be excluded.In a working paper published this month by the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), economists Benjamin Jaros and Joshua Rauh estimate the measure would raise only about $30 billion, with a likely range of $28 billion to $36 billion. That is less than one-third of the revenue forecast by proponents of the tax.According to the researchers, a major reason for the lower estimate is the migration of wealthy residents out of California. The study analysed Forbes billionaire rankings, real estate records and public relocation announcements to conclude that billionaire departures have already reduced the potential tax base by nearly 30%.The economists pointed to several high-profile billionaires who have publicly moved from California, including Peter Thiel and Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin. Together, seven billionaires who have announced relocations account for an estimated $540 billion in wealth, according to the study.The Stanford-affiliated economists argue that the larger issue is not the initial tax collection but the potential long-term loss of income tax revenue if wealthy residents continue leaving the state. The study estimates billionaire departures could reduce California's annual income tax collections by between $1 billion and $3.5 billion. If those losses persist indefinitely, they would outweigh the one-time wealth tax proceeds by approximately $38.9 billion in present-value terms.To test various outcomes, the researchers ran 100,000 simulations using different assumptions for revenue generation and discount rates. They found that 85% of scenarios resulted in a net financial loss for the state. The findings represent a more pessimistic outlook than an earlier analysis from the Hoover Institution, which projected roughly $40 billion in revenue and a net loss of about $25 billion.The economists’ main explanation is that billionaires can leave. Using Forbes rankings, real estate reports and public relocation announcements, they estimate that departures have already eliminated nearly 30 percent of the proposed tax base. CBS News, citing the study, reported that seven billionaires who have publicly moved out of California account for about $540 billion in wealth, including Peter Thiel and Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin. The estimate also discounts the remaining base for the risk that courts strike the tax down. The new figure is a sharper downgrade than the authors’ earlier Hoover analysis, which projected about $40 billion in revenue and a $25 billion net loss.Not all economists share the Stanford researchers' conclusions. A separate study by economists Jasper Boll, Emmanuel Saez and Gabriel Zucman, also published through the NBER, argued that even if every billionaire permanently left California, it would take around 25 years for lost income tax collections to equal the projected $100 billion windfall from the tax. The authors also challenged the assumption that billionaire departures would have permanent effects. They argued that if California does not introduce recurring wealth taxes, some billionaires could eventually return, while newly created fortunes could replenish the state's billionaire population.Meanwhile, California's nonpartisan Legislative Analyst's Office has offered a more moderate forecast, estimating the measure could raise tens of billions of dollars over several years while reducing annual income tax revenue by less than $1 billion.The proposal has triggered one of California's most expensive ballot fights. According to campaign finance disclosures cited by reports, technology billionaires have contributed more than $340 million to oppose the measure and support competing ballot initiatives. Sergey Brin alone has reportedly donated more than $100 million, while other donors include former Google chief executive Eric Schmidt, Palantir co-founder Peter Thiel, Stripe chief executive Patrick Collison and DoorDash CEO Tony Xu. Opponents have spent at least $21.2 million during the first 19 days of September, according to the report.California Governor Gavin Newsom has also opposed the billionaire tax, arguing it could encourage wealthy residents to leave the state along with their income tax payments. Earlier this month, Newsom endorsed Proposition 42, a competing ballot measure backed by Brin that would effectively block Proposition 40 by banning new state taxes on personal property and retroactive taxation.
Article Summary: Measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of California residents who were billionaires as of 1 January 2026. Supporters claim it could raise about $100 billion for the state, around 90% of which would be directed toward healthcare spending. In a working paper published this month by the National Bureau of Economic Research, economists Benjamin Jaros and Joshua Rauh estimate the measure would raise only about $30 billion, with a likely range of $28 billion to $36 billion. According to the researchers, a major reason for the lower estimate is the migration of wealthy residents out of California.

Article Title: He co-founded Facebook with Mark Zuckerberg, later became CEO of work management company but Dustin Moskovitz says ‘top job’ is not for him
Article Text:
Putting on a Mask in a ‘chaotic world’

The Rise of the ‘Accidental Manager’

Poll Vote & Share your view Should companies provide formal management training to all employees? Definitely, it's essential Only for those in leadership roles No, experience is enough I don't have an opinion 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

While some corporate leaders want to run boardrooms, many others end up in executive suites almost entirely by chance. Dustin Moskovitz, however, has a different view on getting the top job. The millennial entrepreneur co-founded Facebook alongside his Harvard roommate Mark Zuckerberg, served as the social network’s very first CTO, and later departed in 2008 to launch the workplace collaboration platform Asana. Moskovitz guided Asana as its CEO for well over a decade and built it into a $3 billion enterprise before stepping down from the top role last year. Yet, looking back at his tenure, Moskovitz admitted that holding the top corporate post was never truly his calling.“I just found it quite exhausting,” Moskovitz said in an interview with Stratechery, candidly describing himself as an introvert. “I don’t like to manage teams. I’d intended to be more of an independent or head of engineering… Then one thing led to another and I was CEO for 13 years,” he confessed, explaining that managing staff had never been his goal—even after creating Asana with co-founder Justin Rosenstein.Operating as CEO required Moskovitz to project an outward persona that went against his personal preferences, creating what he described as the daily grind of having to “put on this face day after day.”Initially, he hoped that leading the company would become less taxing as Asana expanded, thinking that wider operational delegation would eventually let him step back and direct company strategy from behind the scenes. In reality, the day-to-day experience moved in the opposite direction.External social and political upheaval increasingly pulled his attention away from traditional product and company development:“The world just kept getting more chaotic—the first Trump presidency and the pandemic and all the race stuff—it made it just a lot less of the company building, being a CEO is a lot more reacting to problems and doing this sort of thing,” Moskovitz explained.Moskovitz's reluctance to manage mirrors an increasingly common dilemma across corporate workplaces. Fortune cited workplace studies indicating that as many as 82% of bosses fall into the category of "accidental managers." Most received zero formal management instruction and were elevated into supervisory positions simply because they excelled at the technical, functional tasks of their original roles. Because they were strong individual performers, companies routinely promoted them to guide others, even if they had no people-management instincts or desire to lead.
Article Summary: Dustin Moskovitz co-founded Facebook alongside his Harvard roommate Mark Zuckerberg. He later left the social network to launch workplace collaboration platform Asana. He guided Asana as its CEO for well over a decade and built it into a $3 billion enterprise.

Article Title: Days after merger with Warner Bros, Skydance offers employees voluntary buyout; makes 5-day work-from-office compulsory across company; read full memo
Article Text:
In-Person Collaboration

Voluntary Buyout Program

Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreitz are overhauling the company’s corporate culture and cost structure, mandating a full five-day return to the office while launching a voluntary buyout programme for employees. The directives, detailed in an internal staff memo obtained by Deadline, mark the first major operational shake-up since Skydance finalised its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery weeks ago.Under the new policy, employees will be required to work on-site five days a week, phased in over time depending on location. The mandate aligns the broader workforce with Paramount-Skydance, which had already ended hybrid arrangements, while ending the three-day in-office model previously held at Warner Bros. Discovery. The transition will primarily affect major hubs in Los Angeles, New York, Atlanta, and London.“We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people,” Ellison and Kreitz wrote in the memo. “We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them.”Alongside the in-office mandate, leadership introduced a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program aimed at reducing headcount as the company tackles a daunting balance sheet.The merged entity is saddled with nearly $90 billion in debt amid a climate of rising interest rates. Ellison has pledged to deliver at least $2 billion in cost savings, with significant reductions expected to come from layoffs.“As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that,” the memo stated. “To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program. Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer. ”Eligible employees are expected to receive their buyout packages in the coming days as Skydance accelerates its post-merger integration. Here's the full memo as it appeared in Deadline:Team,At Skydance, our goal is to build the next-generation media and entertainment company, powered by creativity and technology. We are creative-first, audience focused, tech-forward and globally scaled. And in a world of endless choice and fierce competition for attention, we don’t just want to succeed. We want to win.To do that, we must be a strong, connected and agile company. Among our business and creative priorities, none matters more than building a strong culture, because it’s the foundation of everything we want to achieve. Winning requires us to work as one team: one company, fully aligned. That means communicating openly and collaborating efficiently across every part of the organization.We believe in-person collaboration is vital to our culture and to the success of our business. Especially in a creative company like ours, the best ideas come from people in the same room, sharing perspectives, challenging one another and solving problems. Being together isn’t just about showing up. It’s about inspiring one another, learning and coaching, forming friendships and having the casual conversations that spark something great.With that in mind, we will adopt a five-day in-office policy across all of Skydance. We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people. We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them.While many of you are already in the office five days a week, we understand this may be a significant change to the daily routines of others. To give you time to plan and adjust, we will take a phased approach by location. You will receive ample notice before changes take effect, and we will work closely with managers to support you through the transition.As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that. To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program. Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer.We recognize this is a significant decision, and we want you to feel informed and supported. If this applies to you, please review your materials carefully and reach out to your leadership or HR representative with any questions. FAQs and other resources are available on the Skydance Integration or Ask Employee Connection on WBD One.Please know we don’t take any of this lightly. We are clear about what we’re building: a company that tells the stories people around the world love, embraces new ways to connect with audiences, and leads the next era of media and entertainment. Article Title: Chinese researchers set optical fiber world record with speed equal to downloading 20,000 4K movies in one second

Spatial division multiplexing and multi-band transmission

A joint research initiative in China has set a new world record for real-time data transmission across optical fiber, reaching a staggering 3.2 petabits per second (Pb/s) over a 24-core cable. The breakthrough achieves data throughput fast enough to download more than 20,000 4K movies in a single second, according to an announcement published on the official government portal for Hubei Province (via Tom’s Hardware). The milestone has been achieved through a collaboration among several leading Chinese technical bodies and optical firms, including the National Key Laboratory of Optical Communication Technology and Network (under the China Information and Communication Technologies Group), Pengcheng Laboratory, and Fiberhome Fujikura Fiber Optic Technology Co., Ltd.The newly-recorded 3.2 Pb/s benchmark surpasses the previous real-time optical transmission record of 2.5 Pb/s set by the very same research coalition earlier this year. That shift represents an almost 30% performance improvement achieved in under 12 months, highlighting rapid progress in high-capacity communication architectures.To put the volume into everyday perspective:From an engineering perspective, the 3.2 Pb/s trial validates the practical viability of combining spatial division multiplexing (SDM) with S+C+L multi-band transmission technology across a multi-core fiber structure.During development, the research team had to navigate significant technical bottlenecks. The first was preventing signals traveling down adjacent cores inside the 24-core line from bleeding into and corrupting one another.The second was managing the distinct transmission behaviors, operational tolerances, and technical specifications across the combined S-, C-, and L-frequency bands simultaneously.What separates this achievement from conventional laboratory benchmarks is its deployment design. The 3.2 Pb/s figure was delivered in real-time using commercially compliant hardware architectures. As the setup adheres to real-world commercial standards, the framework could be practical and deployable across enterprise and public networks in the near future.By contrast, purely academic laboratory trials running across similar 24-core telecommunications cables have charted speeds as high as 5.29 Pb/s. However, those higher theoretical thresholds depend heavily on specialised experimental signal processing techniques and non-standard laboratory equipment.
Article Summary: A joint research initiative in China has set a new world record for real-time data transmission across optical fiber. The breakthrough achieves data throughput fast enough to download more than 20,000 4K movies in a single second. The throughput is approximately 3.2 million times faster than a standard one-gigabit consumer internet line.

Article Title: Japanese companies compensate users after waves of hacking hit business and economic stability
Article Text:
AI hacking (Representative image)

$50 million crypto ransom demanded and rejected

Japanese companies are moving to pay financial compensation directly to affected users following a relentless wave of cyberattacks that has paralysed digital services, compromised customer databases and sparked broader concerns regarding national economic stability. According to a report by news agency Reuters, leading the corporate response, GMO Internet Group, a major digital financial and infrastructure services conglomerate, announced that customers will be fully reimbursed for financial losses resulting from unauthorized access following an attack on its foreign exchange trading platform. Additionally, the company will distribute a goodwill payout of 5,000 yen (around $32) to every customer, group CEO Masatoshi Kumagai revealed.Reflecting on the escalating danger facing online operations, Kumagai issued an assessment of the modern digital landscape.“The internet itself is now starting to break down. The internet is increasingly being transformed into a tool that malicious actors use to threaten and rob people,” wrote Kumagai, whose business footprint spans internet infrastructure, web domains, and cryptocurrency trading platforms.In an update published on Monday (October 26), Kumagai revealed that the suspected hackers behind the breach issued a financial extortion demand, threatening to publicly leak confidential corporate records and customer data unless the company paid $50 million in cryptocurrency.GMO stated that it will not give in to the extortion demand and is coordinating its incident response closely with law enforcement and regulatory authorities. The company did not draw any link between its breach and the PHP software vulnerabilities that forced public portals offline worldwide last week.Beyond financial payouts, GMO plans to offer a complimentary alternative service to clients for six months. While white-hat security researchers contracted by the firm had previously identified system weaknesses, Kumagai acknowledged that the depth and velocity of internal remediation were insufficient to head off the intrusion.Meanwhile, the mounting corporate fallout has drawn a response from Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, who confirmed that the administration plans to compile an emergency package of counter-cyberattack measures by next week. As part of a defensive strategy, the government announced that it will establish a specialised unit tasked with simulating AI-driven attacks to expose structural flaws across enterprise and public networks before malicious actors can weaponize them.The initiative follows widespread domestic disruption after critical bugs disclosed in the foundational PHP language triggered millions of automated exploitation attempts globally.Kumagai urged Tokyo to take an aggressive stance under its newly established cyberdefense framework, which took effect this month. Such countermeasures could include offensive actions, such as targeting hostile external command servers to disable threats at their source.

The company will distribute a goodwill payout of 5,000 yen (around $32) to every customer, group CEO Masatoshi Kumagai revealed.

Article Title: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees in India, US, UK and Canada; HR head Amy Coleman tells staff: Eligible employees will receive an email with...
Article Text:
"This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support,"

"another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs,"

Microsoft's voluntary exit offer pays out like its standard severance

Buyouts now sit alongside layoffs in Microsoft's AI-era job cuts

Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees across India, the US, the UK and Canada, its second voluntary exit programme this year and a much wider one than the first. Announced on Monday in a memo from Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, the Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) covers more than a quarter of the company's roughly 223,000 employees. It reaches up to level 70 on Microsoft's internal scale, which takes in general managers and some staff with vice president titles, though not corporate vice presidents.Unlike the retirement buyout Microsoft ran earlier this year, this one has no age or tenure cut-off, and performance plays no part in who qualifies. Eligible employees will get an email with their individual terms within hours. They have until the first week of December to decide, and those who accept will leave at the end of the year.Coleman wrote. It also gives participating organisationsshe added.The package matches Microsoft's standard severance. That means base pay linked to tenure and level, continued stock vesting, healthcare for a fixed period and career transition support. What it leaves out is the extended healthcare that made the retirement programme an easy yes for many long-serving staff.Severance in Microsoft's US layoffs earlier this year started at 60 days of base pay and went up to 39 weeks for most employees. Staff at level 64 and below got a week of base pay for every six months of service, while levels 65 to 67 got two weeks.Not every team is in. Business leaders decide whether their groups participate, and sales is sitting this one out. Marketing, commercial business, security, and discovery and quantum teams are excluded too, according to people familiar with the matter. Copilot, CoreAI, Windows + Devices, Xbox, finance and HR are among those taking part, while Cloud + AI and Microsoft AI are partially in.The VEO builds on the Voluntary Retirement Program from this spring, the first in Microsoft's history. That offer went to roughly 8,750 US employees at senior director level and below whose age and years at the company added up to at least 70. About 30% took it, and Microsoft booked a $900 million charge for it in April.The turnout helped shrink the layoffs that followed, Coleman said later. Microsoft still cut 4,800 jobs in July, about 2% of its workforce, and several hundred more in September, after cutting over 15,000 in 2025. Headcount stood at 223,000 on June 30, down from 228,000 a year earlier.The company is under pressure to hold down operating costs while it spends tens of billions on data centres and AI infrastructure. Still, Microsoft says the buyout is not a sign it needs fewer people, nor a replacement for layoffs, which remain on the table. It expects a much smaller share of employees to accept this time.Quarterly earnings on Wednesday could offer a first look at what the offer will cost. Coleman called the programme "new for us" in her memo, and said in July that Microsoft was studying whether voluntary exits could become a regular, even annual, fixture. How many of these 60,000 employees take the deal will likely settle that.
Article Summary: Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees across India, the US, the UK and Canada. It is its second voluntary exit programme this year and a much wider one than the first. Eligible employees will get an email with their individual terms within hours.
